measured_justification: The reduction kernels are two-stage (partial -> combine) designed for large-N on-device reductions. The portfolio/execution workloads in this milestone operate on small candidate-set arrays (<= a few hundred names) and per-scenario Monte-Carlo PnL where the VaR/ES reduction is a trivial numpy quantile — binding the GPU reduction kernels for these would be an ARTIFICIAL/REDUNDANT operational call (explicitly disallowed by §19). They remain compiled + pipeline-callable; binding is deferred until a genuine large-N reduction workload exists (e.g. full-universe cross-sectional statistics or large-scenario tail moments).
honesty: Reported separately from consumed kernels; operational kernel count is NOT inflated by redundant calls.
